solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pedant needs adhesive label edge hidden

indicators.note: the letter is tucked away inside the other word, so it is hidden there

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive, a thing that sticks to a surface

indicators.note: the edge of the word label is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone fussy insists a sticky label must have its edge tucked out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' puts L, the leading edge of 'label', inside STICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness about rules and details, the defining trait of a pedant.

clue.text: Wild animal heard in forest

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the words for the animal are spoken

parts.note: a tiger is a wild animal, a big cat

explanation.surface: A wild beast can be heard somewhere in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiga is the subarctic coniferous forest stretching across Siberia and Canada, so it is a type of forest.

clue.text: Say something about role division

indicators.note: about means the words for saying something go around the other piece

parts.note: to say something is to comment
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Someone offers a remark on how roles are divided up.
explanation.definitionFit: A compartment is a separate section, one of the divisions of a larger space such as a train carriage.

clue.text: Sweet medicine swallowed up in some water

indicators.note: swallowed means the medicine goes inside the water
in a down clue up means the whole construction reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pool is some water

indicators.note: in this down entry the word in, set beside up, also turns the medicine upside down before it goes in

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: A dose of medicine is swallowed while taking in some water.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' turns the whole construction over; equivalently each piece reads upwards, LOOP holding LLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard candy on a stick, a type of sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Lose Iraq pursuit badly and it speaks for itself

indicators.note: badly means the letters of these three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Losing a chase into Iraq badly is an obvious failure that needs no comment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal maxim translates literally as 'the thing speaks for itself', used when negligence is evident.

clue.text: Troubles the Financial Times to take a wrong step

indicators.note: to take means the paper's pronoun holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: the clue appears in the Financial Times, so the paper refers to itself as us

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of step are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Something bothers the newspaper into making a misstep.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT setter's 'the Financial Times' means the paper referring to itself as 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsets is a verb meaning disturbs or distresses, the same sense as troubles.

clue.text: See 7
Marine creature lookin' to eat you ultimately

indicators.note: to eat means the searching word takes in the other letter

parts.note: lookin' is a dropped-g looking, so searchin' with its g dropped

indicators.note: ultimately points at the closing letter of you

explanation.surface: A sea creature on the lookout for a meal comes to eat you in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'lookin'' tells you to drop the G from SEARCHING too. 'to eat' puts U, the last letter of 'you', inside SEARCHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea urchins are spiny echinoderms living on the seabed, so they are marine creatures.

clue.text: Name of 7 where Athene, age questionable, originated

indicators.note: questionable means the letters are not settled in the given order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea is named after where the goddess Athene was born, though her age is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the first word of 7-down, SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is a named body of water between Greece and Turkey, so it is the name of a sea.

clue.text: Laid back about S&M being horrible

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the other two letters
laid back means the word laid is written backwards

parts.note: S&M is written as the two letters SM

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed about sadomasochism finds it horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' looks like 'relaxed', but 'back' is the reversal signal on 'Laid' and 'about' wraps the result around S&M.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means dreadful or wretched, a synonym of horrible in its loose sense of very bad.

clue.text: Society values philosopher

parts.note: values as a verb means rates or assesses

explanation.surface: A society holds a philosopher in high esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the classical Athenian thinker who taught Plato.

clue.text: In Paris, it's OK to be bubbly

parts.note: ça is French for it or that, as spoken in Paris
va completes the French ça va, meaning it's OK

explanation.surface: In Paris, being cheerful and lively is perfectly fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The French greeting ça va means 'it's OK'; run together without its cedilla it spells the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is Spanish sparkling wine, and bubbly is slang for any sparkling wine.

clue.text: Meant to conceal criminal act and got involved

indicators.note: to conceal means the word for meant hides the other letters within it

parts.note: to have implied something is to have meant it without saying it

indicators.note: criminal means the letters of act are bent into a crooked order

explanation.surface: Someone intended to cover up a crime and so became caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges 'act' to CAT before 'to conceal' hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be implicated is to be shown to be mixed up in something, often a crime.

clue.text: Read an edition about sound of mathematician

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the sound word
an edition is a new version, so these letters appear in a new arrangement

parts.note: a chime is a ringing sound

explanation.surface: A reader studies a new edition about the sounds a mathematician investigated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edition' rearranges 'Read an' to ARDEAN, which 'about' wraps around the sound word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective formed from Archimedes, the Greek mathematician, describes things belonging to him.

clue.text: Too much God in prayer

indicators.note: in means the god goes inside the word for prayer

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request, a prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: There is an excess of references to God in a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excessive amount, a glut or surplus of something.

clue.text: Lacking energy having crushed the garlic

indicators.note: crushed garlic is broken up, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook feels drained after crushing the garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and listless, without vigour.

clue.text: He's into cooking fancy starters

indicators.note: into means he goes inside the pair of initial letters
starters means taking the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A professional cook enjoys making elaborate appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts HE between C and F, the starters of 'cooking fancy'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional cook whose job is preparing dishes such as elaborate starters.

clue.text: Grandma joke is crude to begin with

parts.note: the tail of this word, after the definition, is ma, a mother
a jest is a joke

indicators.note: to begin with points at the opening letters of is and crude

explanation.surface: Grandma tells a joke that is vulgar from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first half of 'Grandma'; the rest of that word gives MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means stately and impressive, the sense of grand as imposing.

clue.text: Flirtation on the phone is an indicator

indicators.note: on the phone means the word for flirtation is heard rather than read

parts.note: playing footsie is flirtation by touching feet under a table

explanation.surface: Flirting during a phone call is a sign of interest.
explanation.walkthrough: The FTSE 100 share index is nicknamed the Footsie.
explanation.definitionFit: The FTSE 100 is a stock-market index, a measure that indicates how the market is doing.

clue.text: Many an egg is not scrambled — cheers!

parts.note: ova is the plural of ovum, an egg

indicators.note: scrambled means the letters of is not are mixed up like eggs

explanation.surface: Plenty of eggs are left unscrambled, to applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like a negation of 'scrambled', but 'is not' is the fodder that 'scrambled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovations are bursts of applause, the cheers of an appreciative crowd.

clue.text: Capital of Kashmir regularly dry perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps means these letters may be arranged otherwise
regularly means taking every other letter of Kashmir

explanation.surface: The capital of Kashmir is usually a dry place, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives AHI from Kashmir; 'perhaps' rearranges AHI with DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Ultimate solution on vacation to change at the end of the eleventh hour?

definitions.text: at the end of the eleventh hour?

indicators.note: to change means these letters swap into a different order
on vacation means the word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A final answer gets altered at the very last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' leaves SN of 'solution'; 'to change' rearranges ULTIMATE with SN.
explanation.definitionFit: Done right before a deadline, in the final sixty seconds before the clock strikes.

clue.text: Function about university level

indicators.note: about means the event word goes around the university letters

parts.note: a function is a social event
OU is the Open University

explanation.surface: A university event is about levelling up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University (OU) is the UK's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: To even out is to make flat or equal, to level off.

clue.text: Stand inside to take a selfie

indicators.note: inside means the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Go indoors to snap a photo of yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that supports a painter's canvas, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Not aware of Signor Antonio

indicators.note: of means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone does not know about an Italian gentleman named Antonio.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, unaware of a fact.

clue.text: See 22
Believer is first to follow article

indicators.note: to follow means the first piece comes after the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
first is written 1st, read as the letters IST

explanation.surface: A believer is the first to follow a written creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST, with the 1 read as I, gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God or gods.

clue.text: Put an end to drink

definitions.meaning: to put an end to a rumour or plan is to quash it

explanation.surface: Stop someone drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch means to quash, and Scotch is whisky from Scotland.

clue.text: Little money in bank of late

indicators.note: in means the coin goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a small coin, little money

explanation.surface: There's only a little money in the bank lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, not long ago, the same as of late.
